name: Scanlines CRT
basis: why: a beam excites coloured phosphor dots on curved glass; how: barrel distortion, phosphor mask, scanlines, glow, bezel

lumenary.blurb: A curved tube television: phosphor stripes, scanlines, glow and a dark bezel.

facts.bestOn: Bright, colourful pictures and game screenshots

why: A cathode-ray tube draws a picture one line at a time with a beam that excites coloured phosphor dots on a curved glass face. All of that leaves a trace: the bulging shape, visible lines, a texture of colour stripes and a soft glow. Recreating them in turn makes a flat picture feel as if it is glowing from inside a box.
how: For each output pixel work out where it should come from on the flat picture using barrel distortion, which gives the curved face and dark rounded corners.
Multiply in the phosphor mask, which makes every third column favour red, green or blue.
Dim a soft band once per line pair to make the scanlines, then add static.
Add two blurred copies on top for glow.
Finish with a vignette, a glass reflection and a bezel with a rounded window.
history: Karl Ferdinand Braun built the first cathode-ray tube in 1897. Television sets from the 1930s used them, colour sets from the 1950s added three phosphors and a shadow mask, and CRT monitors served computers and consoles into the 2000s before flat panels replaced them. Retro games are still designed around CRT blur and scanlines.
uses: Retro gaming screenshots and capture overlays
Posters with a vintage screen feel
terms: A material that glows when struck by the electron beam.
A bulging warp, strongest at the edges, like looking at a curved screen.
Light that seems to leak around bright areas.
paragraphs: A cathode-ray tube has a curved face, so the picture is bent. For each pixel of the output the program works out where on the flat picture it should come from, using a barrel distortion: the further a point is from the centre, the further out it samples, and the corners fall off the edge of the picture and turn black, which gives the rounded corners. The sampled colour is an interpolation of the four nearest pixels.

Three tube effects are multiplied in. The phosphor mask makes every third column favour red, green or blue (or darkens every third column, for an aperture grille). Scanlines dim a soft band once per line pair. Static is a hash of the pixel position. Finally, two blurred copies are added on top for bloom, then a vignette, a glass reflection and a bezel with a rounded window.

equations.note: Barrel distortion factor; the output pixel at normalised position n samples the source at n·f.
The scanline dip: σ is the scanline slider and p the line period in pixels.

presets.text: Strong curve and scanlines look like an old portable television.
An aperture grille gives the vertical stripe look of a studio monitor.
Switch off the bezel to fill the frame with the tube.
